question: Do a physical |ω| clamp + an anchor-spacing cap (dt_ab < π/ω_hi) cure finite-diff aliasing and invert seed 116, and does the config generalise to slow tumblers?
hypothesis: An |ω| clamp [0.05,1.6] dps + anchor-cap keeps the single-shoot under half a turn so it stops aliasing, inverting 116 and generalising to slow seeds.
narrative_md: A physical |ω| clamp [0.05,1.6] dps + an anchor-spacing cap (dt_ab < π/ω_hi, keeping the A→B finite-diff under half a turn) cure single-shoot aliasing and invert seed 116 as a clean 7-attractor multi-solution set (4 at the surrogate floor; truth at q0 0.19°, ω-dir 0.03°, |ω| 0.1335 vs 0.1336). Anchor-cap mechanism confirmed (single-shoot 145°→0.94°). BUT the slow-tumbler sweep (10/42/31) is BROKEN by a decimation bug that widens 2° cells (truth-near 1.45°→6.61°) + a 6M-vs-1M sampling bug + a padding bug that skipped all polishes — generality unproven. Surrogate-only; truth used only as a label.
